clue.text: 10 put up two million, ignoring banks

indicators.note: put up, in a down clue, says the hidden letters are read upwards, so backwards
ignoring the banks of the phrase means dropping its outer letters, leaving a run from inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tally of two million passengers put up, leaving the banks out of the count.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'ignoring banks' as the definition, but it is the hidden-word signal; the definition is '10', the theme answer TRANSPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch limousine is a means of getting about, a hired car for passengers.

clue.text: Leader of foreign country regularly rearms in battle zone

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a land is a country

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word rearms

explanation.surface: A foreign ruler steadily rearms in a war-torn region.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'rearms' are E, R, S. Flanders, the Belgian region of First World War trenches, is also half of the comedy duo Flanders and Swann, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flanders region saw the great trench battles of the First World War, a byword for a battlefield.

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: in the Australian state of Victoria utility vehicles are utes, a form of transport
NI, Northern Ireland, is the UK's province

explanation.surface: A Victorian-era group joins a tour around a province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' suggests the nineteenth century, but here it means from Victoria in Australia, where a ute is a pick-up truck.
explanation.definitionFit: To join things together is to bring them into union, a straight synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Avoid one in time for discharge

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the word for the period of time

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time
to miss something is to avoid it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice to skip one stint of duty before being let go.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is something given off or released, as from an exhaust: a discharge.

indicators.note: whipped suggests letters beaten into a new shape

explanation.surface: Airline captains are attacked with the butt of a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pistol-whipped' reads as one violent compound, but 'pistol' is the fodder and 'whipped' the anagram signal. 7 is AIRLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Airline commanders are the captains who fly the aircraft, the people at the controls.

indicators.note: the word for set crosses, so contains, the letter for Norway

parts.note: to put something down is to set it
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Transport is ready to sail across to Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed boat poled along a river is a form of water transport.

clue.text: Virgin, perhaps Irish, wearing flared style

indicators.note: the style is worn by, so goes round, the abbreviation for Irish

parts.note: an A-line skirt or dress flares out from a narrow top

explanation.surface: A virgin from Ireland, perhaps, dressed in a flared skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' looks like a person; it is Virgin Atlantic, the airline, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin Atlantic is one example of a company that flies passengers, so the definition is by example.

definitions.meaning: a large volume collecting several works or episodes together
the Latin word is a dative plural meaning for all, as in the original horse-drawn bus

explanation.surface: A bumper volume of a beginner's Latin primer.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is literally Latin for 'for all', and it is also an old name for a bus, fitting the transport theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper edition gathering several books or episodes in one volume is an omnibus edition.

clue.text: Asian capital hasn't managed to progress

indicators.note: hasn't says the word for managed is missing from the city

parts.note: Rangoon, now Yangon, was the capital of Burma
ran, as in ran a business, means managed

explanation.surface: An Asian capital has failed to make progress.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on is to continue or advance, a phrasal synonym for progressing.

clue.text: Hit by 2 and 16 across, new Pathfinder got lost crossing river

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cross, so enclose, the abbreviation for river
new says the letters of the following words are made fresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: A new Pathfinder vehicle got lost while fording a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 and 16 across are FLANDERS and SWANN, the comic duo whose hit song about the London bus has this title. 'got lost' looks like the anagram signal, but both words are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a famous Flanders and Swann comic song celebrating the London double-decker bus.

clue.text: A very quiet part of London's attractive

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet
Ealing is a borough of west London

explanation.surface: A hushed corner of London is charming.
explanation.walkthrough: EALING is a west London borough, famous for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with appeal draws people in, so it is pleasing or attractive.

indicators.note: on, as in on board a vessel, puts the leader inside the ship

parts.note: board stands for the ship you go on board, the steamship abbreviation
to have led is to have been in charge

explanation.surface: Transport was in charge on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention for going inside a ship's abbreviation, steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledges pulled over snow are a means of carrying people and goods.

indicators.note: injured suggests the word was is damaged into a new order

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A lover got hurt in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is an old poetic word for a young suitor or sweetheart.

clue.text: Line in religious writing by Hardy that's deleted another line

indicators.note: in puts the letter for line inside the religious writing

parts.note: pi is short for pious, so religious
MS, manuscript, is a piece of writing

indicators.note: deleted says the abbreviation for that is is struck from the name

parts.note: Ollie was Oliver Hardy of Laurel and Hardy
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A line in a scripture by Thomas Hardy was crossed out and replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' at the start is wordplay, not the definition; the definition is the clue's end. Hardy is not the novelist but Oliver Hardy, nicknamed Ollie.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plimsoll line on a ship's hull marks the safe loading depth, so it is one more kind of line.

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for sad is thrown away

parts.note: sorry means sad, regretful

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician's gloomy leader has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: LORRY is the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A large goods vehicle is a means of road haulage.

indicators.note: scratching the head strikes out the first letter

parts.note: Ivan the Terrible was the archetypal Russian despot

explanation.surface: A tyrant's vehicles have him scratching his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Vans are covered vehicles used for moving goods, a kind of road transport.

parts.note: a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: The pseudonym of the main character in Proust's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen name' looks like a pseudonym, but pen is a female swan. Charles Swann is the central figure of Proust's 'Swann's Way'; Donald Swann is also the theme's half of Flanders and Swann.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Swann is the leading figure of the first volume of Proust's great novel.

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the pieces go inside the word for understand

parts.note: to see is to understand
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: Transport, I gather, is a dull plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft able to land on water is a means of air transport.

parts.note: ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Transport is roughly right.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart is a horse-drawn vehicle for carrying loads.

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh

explanation.surface: County Clare ordered some small boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County Clare' reads as the Irish county; CO is the abbreviation and Clare the fodder for 'ordered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coracles are small round wicker boats, a form of river transport.

clue.text: Touching a female in Indian dress after game

parts.note: on means touching, as in on the table

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the dress

parts.note: a sari is a draped garment worn by Indian women

explanation.surface: A tender moment with a woman in a sari after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like a sporting fixture; it means wild animals hunted or watched.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on safari is out tracking wild animals, that is pursuing big game.

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is cut

parts.note: Abe was Abraham Lincoln's nickname

indicators.note: so-called says the word is as it is called, said out loud

parts.note: to have ducked something is to have escaped it

explanation.surface: Lincoln all but slipped away from a so-called kidnapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to carry someone off by force, a sinister kind of conveying from place to place.

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so one piece goes inside the name

parts.note: taken as the name Fry
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Elizabeth Fry, the prison reformer, tending a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth Fry was the English prison reformer; the name is split so that 'Elizabeth' gives ER and 'Fry' holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry is a boat carrying passengers across a stretch of water.

parts.note: Fats Waller was the celebrated jazz pianist

indicators.note: climbing, in a down clue, says the word goes upwards, so backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, ideal, written here with the letter I

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist's perfect climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing shrub' looks like one phrase, but 'climbing' is the reversal signal; the plant is not a climber.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatsia is an evergreen shrub with large glossy leaves, often grown indoors.

indicators.note: up-and-coming, in a down clue, says the hidden letters are read upwards
entertained says the words hold the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rising Cole Porter entertained passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'entertained' as the definition; it is the hidden-word signal, and the definition is '10', TRANSPORT, of which an Opel car is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Opel is a German car maker, so its cars are a type of road vehicle.

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the end

parts.note: a scab is a worker who crosses a picket line

explanation.surface: The first non-striker to finish takes the taxis.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabs are taxis, hired cars that carry passengers.

parts.note: BEA, British European Airways, was a former airline
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An old airline runs transport.
explanation.walkthrough: BEA merged into British Airways in 1974. 'Bear' here is the verb, to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear is to carry, as in bearing a load, which is what transporting means.

clue.text: Kit is able to enter "Come Dancing"

indicators.note: the word for is able enters the rearranged letters
dancing has the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: A kit is able to get onto a television ballroom show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come Dancing' was a long-running BBC ballroom dancing programme; 'Dancing' is the anagram signal for COME, giving MECO.
explanation.definitionFit: Meccano is a construction set of metal strips and bolts, a classic model-building kit.

indicators.note: to collect means to take in the papers
round says the word is turned about

parts.note: races are dashes, sprints
ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: Transport rushes round to pick up some documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashes' looks like punctuation or hurrying; it is a plural noun for sprints.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a passenger car attached to the side of a motorcycle.
